clue.text: Quickly becoming aware of standing by prince

parts.note: Pr is the standard abbreviation for prince
to be on to something is to have become aware of it

explanation.surface: Someone swiftly realises they are standing next to royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The prince comes first and the awareness sits beside it, so 'standing by' only places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an informal adverb borrowed from Spanish, meaning at once or without delay.

clue.text: Paul oddly exaggerated over feature of baroque art

indicators.note: oddly tells us to keep only the letters in odd-numbered positions of the name

parts.note: first and third letters of the name

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top, meaning exaggerated

explanation.surface: A critic complains that a man called Paul overdid things when describing baroque decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A putto is a chubby naked cherub figure, a common decorative element in baroque painting and sculpture.

clue.text: Occupied during trip

parts.note: over can mean during, as in 'over the weekend'
a run is a short journey or trip

explanation.surface: A seat or room was taken while someone was away on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A territory that has been overrun has been invaded and taken over, that is occupied by a force.

clue.text: Cover prohibition with article on American boss

parts.note: a top is a lid or cover
a ban is a prohibition
the indefinite article
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An instruction to conceal a ban, plus some article about an American employer.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is informal slang for the most important person in an organisation, the person in charge.

clue.text: Single daughter extremely gullible when nervous

parts.note: single means one
D is the abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters only

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: An only daughter who is very easily fooled becomes anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge is an idiom for being tense, jumpy or anxious.

clue.text: Jack heard about Italian leader being innocent

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece wraps the other
heard means we want a word that sounds like the card name, not its spelling

parts.note: the jack in a pack of cards is also called the knave; spoken, it is the church's nave

indicators.note: a leader is at the front, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: first letter of Italian

explanation.surface: Jack overheard talk about an Italian chief and seemed blameless.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent K of knave disappears in speech, leaving NAVE, which goes around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive describes someone lacking experience or guile, so innocent is a close synonym.

clue.text: Worked on small vehicle kept inside shed

indicators.note: kept inside means these pieces are held within the other word

parts.note: to do a job is to work on it
S is the abbreviation for small
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone tinkered with a little car stored in a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like the building where the car is kept, but it is the verb, meaning get rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed something is to cast it off, which is what discard means as a verb.

clue.text: Basic design of metal eel maintaining hint of naturalism

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the jumble keeps one letter within it
a design is a new arrangement, so these letters are laid out in a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: a hint is just a small taste, so only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: first letter of naturalism

explanation.surface: A simple sculpture of a metal eel that keeps a touch of natural realism.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means fundamental or rudimentary, relating to first principles, so basic is a synonym.

clue.text: Dante regularly ignored allure of crack

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter is dropped, keeping the ones in between

parts.note: second and fourth letters of the poet's name
to allure is to tempt

explanation.surface: A reader often passed over Dante, yet felt drawn to tackle him.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a crack at something is to try it, so crack as a noun means an attempt.

clue.text: Note by Rex on manuscript describing popular place of worship

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript
in means fashionable or popular
te is a note of the sol-fa scale
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king writes a note in a manuscript about a much-visited church.
explanation.definitionFit: A minster is a large or important church, often one that began as part of a monastery, such as York Minster.

clue.text: Villain's crimes affected social worker

indicators.note: affected means disturbed or altered, so the letters are moved out of place

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
the ant is a social insect and a classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A criminal's offences have had an impact on a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' looks like a job in social services, but it means an insect living in a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer, someone who behaves badly or criminally, so villain is a synonym.

clue.text: Visit country to get largely unfamiliar gemstone

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the final letter of the word is cut

parts.note: to tour a place is to visit it
Mali is a country in West Africa
something new is unfamiliar

explanation.surface: Travel abroad to acquire an exotic precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourmaline is a crystalline boron silicate mineral cut and polished as a semi-precious jewel.

clue.text: Somewhat degenerate bawd returning to assist in crime

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the run of letters is read right to left
somewhat means only part of the phrase, so the letters are found within it

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A depraved brothel-keeper comes back to help with an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: A bawd is an old word for a woman running a brothel.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to encourage or help someone commit a wrongdoing, a legal term paired with aid.

clue.text: Obsession of academic starts to nullify intellectual awareness

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, an academic degree

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A scholar's fixation threatens to cancel out their understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A mania is an excessive enthusiasm or fixation, so it is a close synonym of an obsession.

clue.text: Small scale version of car found by volunteers back near river

parts.note: the Mini is a classic British car

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A model car turns up next to some volunteers by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniature is a much reduced copy of something, such as a tiny model or painting.

clue.text: Girl overwhelmed by compassion after copper's greed

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swamped or engulfed, so the name sits inside the other word

parts.note: pity is compassion
Di is a short girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman is moved to sympathy by a policeman's avarice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer, but here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupidity is an excessive desire for money or possessions, the same thing as greed.

clue.text: Soldier on parade initially finding hesitation hard to endure

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the word is kept

parts.note: first letter of parade
er is the sound of hesitating
severe conditions are harsh and hard to bear

explanation.surface: A soldier on the parade ground finds it tough to keep going without hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier on' reads as a soldier taking part in a parade; it is the phrasal verb meaning keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is to keep going in spite of difficulty, which is what persevere means.

clue.text: Growth at home to stop around end of year

parts.note: someone at home is in

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the verb wraps the single letter

parts.note: to cease is to stop

indicators.note: end of means only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: last letter of year

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to halt the expansion of their household as the year ends.
explanation.definitionFit: An increase is a rise in size or amount, the same as growth.

clue.text: King became confused and unkempt in appearance

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king
to be addled is to be muddled

explanation.surface: A monarch grew befuddled and let himself go.
explanation.definitionFit: Raddled describes someone looking worn out and dishevelled, as from age or hard living.

clue.text: By no means all declare belief in revolt

indicators.note: by no means all says we take just a part of the following words, a stretch of their letters

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Not everyone will profess faith in an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel is to rise up against authority, so the verb revolt is a direct synonym.

clue.text: In Crosby covering a race

indicators.note: covering means lying over and enclosing, so the singer's name goes around the rest

parts.note: Bing Crosby, the American crooner
taken as written
the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race

explanation.surface: A short piece of sports reporting: Crosby is out covering a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition, but in cricket a side that is in is batting.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the team that is in is the one batting, taking its turn to score runs.

clue.text: Deceived over opening of news agency

indicators.note: over means covering, so the verb lies across and encloses the letter

parts.note: to be had is to be tricked

indicators.note: an opening is a start, so only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: first letter of news

explanation.surface: Someone was fooled when a news agency launched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'News agency' reads as one phrase; agency alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a hand in something means taking part in it, so hand can mean agency or involvement.

clue.text: Curt once played around in Paris I guess

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the jumbled letters enclose the French pronoun
played suggests performed freely, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
je is French for I

explanation.surface: A man called Curt once performed in Paris, or so the speaker supposes.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjecture is an opinion formed from incomplete information, which is what a guess is.

clue.text: Rule on first of claims immediately

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the following word is used

parts.note: first letter of claims
anon is an old word for at once

explanation.surface: A judge gives a ruling on the first claims straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a general rule or principle, as in church law or the canons of good taste.

clue.text: Frank's dog runs for hours

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one abbreviation swaps out the other

parts.note: a hound is a hunting dog
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
H is the abbreviation for hours

explanation.surface: A man called Frank has a dog that runs about for hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank's' looks like the dog's owner, but it is the definition followed by 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Round, as in a round rebuke, means plain-spoken and candid, which is a sense of frank.

clue.text: Summarise existing course of action

parts.note: out can mean available or in existence, as in 'the best car out'
a line is a policy or course, as in the party line

explanation.surface: Give a brief account of the policy currently in place.
explanation.definitionFit: To outline something is to give its main points without detail, a brief summary.

clue.text: Curious desire to protect Updike's source remains

indicators.note: to protect means to shield, so the jumble surrounds one letter
curious means odd or strange, so the letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the first letter of the name is used

parts.note: first letter of Updike, the American novelist

explanation.surface: An odd wish to safeguard the source of a writer's surviving papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left over after the rest has gone, so it is a synonym of the noun remains.

clue.text: Workers losing bit of momentum before strike's conclusion

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: workers are men in crossword convention

indicators.note: a bit of the word is just its first letter

parts.note: first letter of momentum, the letter removed
to ding is to hit or strike

explanation.surface: Industrial action ends as the workforce loses its drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests a walkout by the workers, but it means a blow; the 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is the final part of something, its conclusion.

clue.text: Poseidon perhaps in love captured by Degas dancing

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so the letter is enclosed by the jumble
dancing letters move about, ending up in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
love is zero in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: A Greek god in love is painted among Degas's ballet dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon was the Greek ruler of the oceans, an example of a deity of the sea, hence 'perhaps'.
